draft.title: Reproduction in flowering plants
card: Pollen is made in the anther. It is carried to the stigma of a flower by wind or by animals such as bees and birds. This move is called pollination.
A pollen grain grows a tube down to an ovule in the ovary. A male gamete from the pollen joins the egg inside the ovule. This is fertilisation.
After fertilisation, the ovule becomes a seed. The ovary becomes a fruit that holds the seed or seeds.
Many plants also grow new plants without seeds. Runners are stems that grow along the soil, and bulbs are underground food stores. Both can grow into new plants.
draft.remember: Pollen lands on the stigma, fertilises an ovule, and the ovule becomes a seed. Runners and bulbs make new plants without seeds.

a.q: In a flowering plant, what does an ovule become after it is fertilised?
a.why: Fertilisation joins a male gamete with the egg in the ovule, and the ovule then becomes a seed. The fruit is tempting, but the fruit grows from the ovary, which holds the seeds.
a.clue: The ovule is inside the ovary.

b.q: Sam grows a strawberry plant in Perth. It sends out long stems along the soil, and a new plant grows from each stem. Which statement explains how the new plants form?
opts: The stems are runners, which grow new plants without seeds
The stems carry pollen, which fertilises a new ovule
The stems are bulbs, which store seeds for the new plants
The stems are fruits, which hold the seeds of new plants
b.why: Stems that grow along the soil and make new plants are runners. They do this without seeds, pollen or fertilisation. The fruit option is tempting, but a fruit grows from the ovary after fertilisation and is not a stem.
b.clue: Does a runner need pollen to make a new plant?

b.best: The stems are runners, which grow new plants without seeds
